title: Policy stitch failure — hypothesis journal
content:
Context / quick summary:
- During the 2026-03-09 22:xx UTC incident we saw a cluster of mid-latency errors where requests were repeatedly failing to transition to fallback model variants. The client saw 504s after ~8s (timeout at edge).
- Symptoms: route-decision logs show two successive policy evaluations but the final routing table returned an empty candidate set ("no compatible endpoints") for ~1.5 minutes for a subset of request IDs.
- Scope: ~0.6% of traffic for org tenant: acme-enterprise-prod, mostly long-seq chat requests from eu-west-1 that got proxied to us-east-1 for model variant fallback.

Raw snippets (sanitized):
- route-decision log (one sample request):
  timestamp=2026-03-09T22:14:05.123Z  req_id=req-8f3b2a  src_region=eu-west-1  policy_chain=[latencySLO,quotaAware,modelVariantFallback]  candidates_pre=[eu-west-1-a(usermodel-v2), eu-west-1-b(usermodel-v2), us-east-1-a(usermodel-v1-q8)]  candidates_post=[ ]  decision=NO_ENDPOINTS  reason="constraints_unmet:compatibility-mismatch"

- edge error seen by client: 
  HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
  x-rw-req: req-8f3b2a
  x-rw-route-code: NO_ENDPOINTS

- runtime stack snippet (from dedicated pool leader):
  2026-03-09T22:14:05.120Z ERROR rider-reconciler: failed to apply route set: verification failed: model-compatibility-check: missing-tokenizer-mapping for model "usermodel-v1-q8"

Commands I ran during repro attempts (local dev env + staging):
- curl to decision API to replay header & body:
  curl -X POST \"https://staging-routing.redwood.internal/decide\" \"-H 'x-rw-tenant: acme-enterprise-prod' -d '@sample-long-chat.json' -v

- checked routing config in k8s configmap (staging):
  kubectl -n routing get configmap routing-policy -o yaml | sed -n '1,200p'

- repro with routing simulator (python script):
  python tools/simulate_routing.py --policy-chain latencySLO,quotaAware,modelVariantFallback --src-region eu-west-1 --payload samples/long-chat.json

Observations from runs:
- When the modelVariantFallback node runs after quotaAware it expects a translated compatibility tuple (cpu/gpu/quant) in the candidates metadata. In prod logs the tuple is missing for certain us-east-1 pool endpoints (appears when we moved to q8 quantized variants last week).
- Staging replicas that had the new quantized model show compatibility metadata; older pools have a missing field `tokenizer_profile`. The compatibility check code treats missing fields as incompatible (correct), but policy stitch expects a fallback to region with variant mapping, not "no endpoints".
- The difference: policy-chain merging code in router merges candidate lists by intersection for strict policies. If a later policy (compatibility) filters all, router should attempt to relax earlier policies (e.g., relax region affinity) — that relaxation seems skipped when quotas are present.

Hypothesis 1 (policy-stitch ordering bug):
- When quotaAware policy marks a candidate as "quota-hard" (reserved capacity hit) it tags candidate with reason=quota_full but leaves the candidate in the list. The compatibility check later removes it (missing tokenizer). Instead of backtracking and removing quota constraint, the stitcher does not consider alternate candidates from other regions because of an early short-circuit in the policy-merge reducer (specifically in router/policy/stitcher.go lines ~210-230).
- Expected: router should run an incremental relaxation pass: if intersection is empty, try pairwise union with relaxed flags (drop quotaHard, then drop regionPreference).

Hypothesis 2 (metadata propagation regression after rollout of q8 builds):
- During the q8 rollout last week we updated the model bootstrap script which registers model metadata to control-plane. A race between bootstrap and health-check can leave a model endpoint registered but without tokenizer_profile populated for a short window. The router's fast path doesn't tolerate missing tokenizer_profile and results in empty candidate set.
- Expected mitigation: make router tolerant (treat missing tokenizer_profile as "pending" and prefer endpoints with it) or ensure bootstrap writes metadata atomically.

Small repro plan (minimal blast radius):
1) Simulate scenario with routing simulator: bring up 3 fake endpoints: eu1(v2 full metadata), eu2(v2 limited metadata), us1(v1-q8 missing tokenizer_profile). Run policy-chain replicate and assert decision NO_ENDPOINTS.
2) Patch stitcher locally to perform union fallback (quick hack): change reducer from strict intersection to try intersections then unions (flag controlled by ENV). Run simulator and confirm route resolution picks us1 when region affinity relaxed.
3) Add extra log fields: include full candidate metadata in route-decision logs (masked sensitive fields) to make postmortem easier.
4) For production rollback: add temporary fail-open for tokenizer_profile check for one hour for affected tenants while we patch bootstrap.

Notes on telemetry / dashboards to check:
- Per-route decision histogram: counts of NO_ENDPOINTS by tenant and region (timeseries).
- Model metadata drift dashboard: percentage of endpoints missing tokenizer_profile per pool.
- Quota rejects overlap with compatibility rejects: heatmap in 5m windows.

Quick config excerpts (sanitized):
- routing policy snippet (policy-chain):
  - latencySLO: hard=true
  - quotaAware: hard=false
  - modelVariantFallback: hard=true, allowMetadataPending=false

- candidate metadata (expected):
  {
    "endpoint_id": "eu-west-1-a",
    "model": "usermodel-v2",
    "quant": "fp16",
    "tokenizer_profile": "v2-bpe-2026-02-10",
    "region": "eu-west-1"
  }

- candidate metadata (observed problematic):
  {
    "endpoint_id": "us-east-1-a",
    "model": "usermodel-v1-q8",
    "quant": "q8",
    "region": "us-east-1"
  }
  (note: missing tokenizer_profile)

Questions / open items:
- Is there an existing feature flag to enable "relaxed stitcher"? I couldn't find it quickly in flags service (searched for STITCHER_RELAX).
- Who owns the model bootstrap path that writes tokenizer_profile? CC: @Diego and @Ravi — I traced to model-onboard PR #1193 but unsure who released it last week.
- Should we push a 1-hour fail-open on prod for acme-enterprise-prod only? Pros: restores traffic quickly. Cons: risk serving slightly incompatible tokenizer profiles (low probability but needs a quick eval).

Immediate next steps (my plan):
- Today: run simulator + quick hack union patch to validate hypothesis 1. If it fixes, prepare a small prod patch behind a flag.
- Tomorrow: open a follow-up to model bootstrap team to add atomic metadata write + add health-check gating.
- Add temporary alert: if NO_ENDPOINTS > 0.1% for any tenant within 5m, page SRE.

Breadcrumbs (request ids I collected):
- req-8f3b2a (EU long chat)
- req-8f3b99 (EU short chat)
- req-8f4c11 (US fallback attempt)

Mini timeline (UTC):
- 2026-03-09T22:13:58 - increased error rates start for tenant
- 2026-03-09T22:14:05 - first NO_ENDPOINTS recorded (req-8f3b2a)
- 2026-03-09T22:15:12 - SRE alerted for elevated 504s (pager, auto-ack)
- 2026-03-09T22:16:40 - manual failover to older pool reduced errors

Random notes to self:
- check router/policy/stitcher.go and router/policy/reducer_test.go for failing unit tests around empty candidate sets.
- add a deterministic unit test that simulates: quota flagging + missing metadata + region fallback.
- don't forget to mark this doc as ephemeral; will move final write-up to Confluence if we get a clean repro and fix.

If anyone reading: add any stray request ids or debug dumps here. I'll update during the hack.

Maya
